summary.headline: AvenuesAI Q2 FY27 revenue rose 47% YoY to Rs 2,879 crore, but PAT grew only 6% to Rs 72 crore as take rate fell to 5.06 bps.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations for Q2 FY27 rose 47% YoY to Rs 2,879 crore, while operating EBITDA excluding other income was Rs 98.9 crore against Rs 96.2 crore a year earlier. H1 revenue rose 71% to Rs 5,560 crore, but H1 operating cash flow was negative Rs 192 crore, which management attributed mainly to faster merchant settlements. Management said it deliberately prioritised TPV scale over take rate, with net take rate down about 4% QoQ to 5.06 bps. The call emphasised strategic initiatives (Rediff ecosystem, international expansion, Tesco transaction-intelligence/AI) with little quantified near-term return, and several answers were vague.

segments.name: Payments (CC Avenue)
segments.commentary: TPV rose 19% QoQ to Rs 1.77 lakh crore in Q2, but net take rate fell to 5.06 bps as management chose scale over pricing. Management said 38-40% of UPI transactions are currently free, and an MDR on about 3% of UPI volume is expected but not yet implemented.

segments.name: Rediff (ecosystem, AvenuesAI holds ~82%)
segments.commentary: Management said Rediff annualised revenue is upwards of Rs 200 crore and profit is about Rs 100 crore a year, with Rediff Fund the largest profit driver. A confidential DRHP has been filed, with timing left to Rediff's board and markets.

segments.name: International (UAE, Saudi Arabia, Oman; US targeted)
segments.commentary: Management said international margins are much better than India. Licences were obtained in Saudi Arabia and RBI-related approvals were mentioned. No financial quantification was given.

segments.name: Tesco / transaction intelligence (AI)
segments.commentary: Management described it as still being conceptualised and developed, with low odds of success but large potential returns. No revenue or spend was quantified. About Rs 294 crore of the recent issue proceeds was earmarked for AI-related investment, and management said little of it has been deployed so far.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EPS guidance reiterated at Rs 8.75-9.50 per share (slide 11); H1 EPS is about Rs 4.5, and management said it is staying with the guidance.
FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of Rs 11,000-13,000 crore reiterated; H1 revenue of Rs 5,560 crore is about 43-50% of that range.
Management expects an incremental TPV of Rs 50,000-100,000 crore over the next 24 months from partnerships (internal estimate).
Management expects an MDR-related revenue benefit on UPI, with more detail to come by next quarter; no regulatory ceiling or floor was confirmed.
No dividend was announced; management said the board prefers to reinvest earnings for growth.
capex_capacity: About Rs 294 crore of the recent issue proceeds was earmarked for AI-related investment; management said little has been deployed so far and deployment is under review.
Management said it is being conservative on data-centre expansion and expects clearer decisions in the current or next quarter.
Strategic investments in online PSB loans and fintech (e.g. Ratnafin) were described as long-term with no cash flows yet; management did not quantify their size.
A 'Rediff Pay' UPI launch is under way after NPCI onboarding permission in a closed user group (CUG) stage.
demand_pricing: Management said it is deliberately prioritising transaction scale and merchant relationships, accepting take-rate compression.
Management cited new products including Apple Pay, WhatsApp in-stream payments, Ship Rocket checkout, and a step-to-pay device, which it says support growth.
Management said RESavvy hospitality solutions are live with more than 3,000 properties, with channel-manager connections to about 150 websites.
Management said that in the offline payments market, Brazil and China are close to 90% penetration against about 30% in India.

qa_highlights.question: Why did growth slow this quarter, and is it seasonal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was prioritised over take rate to capture volumes ahead of the festive season. The net take rate fell about 4% QoQ to 5.06 bps, and management called it a conscious decision.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 EPS guidance still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated EPS guidance of Rs 8.75-9.50, with H1 at about Rs 4.5 per share.

qa_highlights.question: What are Rediff's revenue and profit contributions and synergy timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rediff annualised revenue is above Rs 200 crore and profit is about Rs 100 crore a year. Synergies may take a few quarters to show up.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any promoter selling, and what is the Rediff IPO timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no promoter selling and that promoters invested in the primary issue. On the Rediff IPO, the timing depends on the Rediff board and markets; a confidential DRHP has been filed and valuation will be set by bankers.

qa_highlights.question: What are the margin trajectory and MDR impacts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said take-rate pressure is real and some margin-accretive levers (UPI MDR, value-added services) could offset it. The MDR impact is not yet quantified, and management expects to report it next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend policy and the Rediff transfer effect on shareholders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the board prefers to reinvest earnings. It said the Rediff business transfer is already complete and fully consolidated, with no additional impact from it.

risks_watch: Operating cash flow was negative Rs 192 crore in H1 because of settlement acceleration; watch working capital and cash conversion.
Net take rate fell about 4% QoQ to 5.06 bps; watch whether competitive pricing continues and whether scale translates into profit.
Q2 PAT growth of 6% against revenue growth of 47% signals thin spreads; management did not give a margin floor.
AI and Tesco investments have no quantified returns, and management described the odds as against them.
Possible UPI MDR implementation timing and its net revenue impact are unclear.
Rediff IPO timing and valuation are undetermined; watch for an update.
Management did not confirm FY27 EPS guidance beyond reiteration; the H2 run-rate needed to reach Rs 8.75-9.50 implies a sharp step-up from H1 (~Rs 4.5).
summary.management_tone: Confident on scale, strategy and the EPS guidance, but noticeably evasive on margins, cash flow, AI returns and the Rediff IPO timeline. Management repeatedly framed take-rate compression as a deliberate choice and gave few quantified targets.
key_quotes: So it's a conscious decision and that scale will potentially open up more opportunities to give services to our merchants and customers.
Our objective is not growth at any cost. Our objective is to build a larger, more diversified and sustainably profitable technology business.
International margins are much better than India.
These are long-term strategic investments they don't contribute to cash flow into the company

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Net take rate fell about 4% QoQ to 5.06 bps and Q2 PAT grew only 6% vs revenue +47%, but management cites UPI MDR (about 3% of UPI volume, not yet implemented) and value-added services as possible offsets, unquantified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 TPV rose 19% QoQ to Rs 1.77 lakh crore and management expects incremental TPV of Rs 50,000-100,000 crore over 24 months from partnerships (internal estimate), with Apple Pay, WhatsApp and Rediff Pay adding reach.

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: New product launch

rows.label: H1 operating cash flow negative Rs 192 crore
rows.why: Management attributed the negative H1 operating cash flow of Rs 192 crore mainly to faster merchant settlements, and cash stood at Rs 546.5 crore at 30 Sep 2026 against equity of Rs 5,145 crore, so cash conversion may stay weak while settlement speed is prioritised.

rows.label: Rediff IPO (confidential DRHP filed)

tone.note: Management was confident on TPV scale, the reiterated Rs 8.75-9.50 EPS guidance and new products, but evasive on margins, MDR quantum, H1 cash flow, AI returns and the Rediff IPO timeline; analysts pressed on the take-rate fall and slow profit growth.
